endorsements.quote: Patients must always know when AI is being used on their health, the benefits and disadvantages of using it, and be given the choice to use it or not (shared decisionmaking process to use AI).
Patients must always know if they are dealing with a human or with an AI.
Even if autonomous Medical-AI is used, humans must always be able to overrun an AI decision.
In the case of a clinical decision being taken by or with the help of AI, patients must have the right to a second opinion where AI is not used.
Healthcare workers must be trained to understand how AI works and be able to take proper decisions using AI.
Healthcare workers must be trained to understand how AI works and be able to take proper decisions using AI.
There should be dynamic informed consent models where participants can withdraw their personal data at any given time for any reason.
An impact assessment should be carried out prior to the implementation of each Medical-AI to make sure benefits outweigh the negative effects of using medical- AI
Ethical reflections and deliberations on the use of Medical-AI must include the environmental impact this technology will have.
We must go beyond establishing who is responsible and accountable and establish proper systems and institutions to make sure patients are compensated for any harm caused by Medical-AI.
Competing interests must be stated by Medical-AI developers for a transparent Medical-AI development.
Medical-AI should only be used in the general population after appropriate medical clinical trials are carried out.
It should be openly stated what population what used to train a certain medical-AI.
Periodic audits on the Medical-AI performance must be done.
Multidisciplinary group evaluations (with patients, or patient advocates, and clinicians) should be used to monitor the Medical-AI performance.
The steering committee recommends these reports be publicly available.
Medical-AI must only be used after an appropriate risk and benefits analysis of the use of Medical-AI is carried out.
Patients should have the opportunity to be involved in data collection for AI development and give their informed consent for specific uses of their data.
Patients must have the right to access their own personal data.

unlisted_practices: Ensure responsibility for medical AI use always remains with humans and institutional actors, shared proportionately among stakeholders according to roles and authority.
Grant patients quality care and continuity of care with adequate alternatives when they voluntarily reject the use of medical AI.
Adapt and validate medical AI to the social, cultural, and endemic context and populations where it is used.
Involve healthcare workers, patients, and other stakeholders in the development of medical AI.
Provide patient and public education on AI.
Include AI courses in medical school curricula.
Implement data protection mechanisms such as data stewardship, encryption, and federated learning for medical AI.
Scientifically validate medical AI and prove it safe before use on humans, using training data that are accurate and validated.
Develop medical AI to mitigate bias and cyber-attacks.
Provide clinicians a contact point for help and for reporting complaints or adverse events with AI tools.
Apply a proportional, risk-based approach to informed consent for AI, with a default expectation of transparency and justified exceptions.
Use a clinician ethical checklist for structured reflection when using medical AI.

screen.reason: This paper presents a formal eDelphi consensus exercise producing best practice guidelines and a clinical bioethics framework for the governance and use of medical AI.
